slides.title: The Lord of the Sabbath does not simply have authority over a day of rest. He has authority to give rest to the soul.

slides.title: The One who calls us to obedience is the same One who invites us to find rest in Him.

slides.title: Because we cannot claim to know the Lord of the Sabbath while refusing to learn from the mercy of the Lord who gives rest.

slideScriptures.text_en:
28 Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
29 Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
30 For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

slideScriptures.text_en: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
slideScriptures.text_es: Acuérdate del día de reposo para santificarlo.
slideScriptures.copyright: Texto bíblico: Reina-Valera 1960 ® © Sociedades Bíblicas en América Latina, 1960. Renovado © Sociedades Bíblicas Unidas, 1988.

slideScriptures.text_en: And remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt, and that the LORD thy God brought thee out thence through a mighty hand and by a stretched out arm: therefore the LORD thy God commanded thee to keep the sabbath day.
slideScriptures.text_es: Acuérdate que fuiste siervo en tierra de Egipto, y que el Señor tu Dios te sacó de allá con mano fuerte y brazo extendido; por lo cual el Señor tu Dios te ha mandado que guardes el día de reposo.
slideScriptures.copyright: Texto bíblico: Reina-Valera 1960 ® © Sociedades Bíblicas en América Latina, 1960. Renovado © Sociedades Bíblicas Unidas, 1988.

slideScriptures.text_en:
1 At that time Jesus went on the sabbath day through the corn; and his disciples were an hungred, and began to pluck the ears of corn and to eat.
2 But when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto him, Behold, thy disciples do that which is not lawful to do upon the sabbath day.
slideScriptures.text_es:
1 En aquel tiempo iba Jesús por los sembrados en un día de reposo; y sus discípulos tuvieron hambre, y comenzaron a arrancar espigas y a comer.
2 Viéndolo los fariseos, le dijeron: He aquí tus discípulos hacen lo que no es lícito hacer en el día de reposo.
slideScriptures.copyright: Texto bíblico: Reina-Valera 1960 ® © Sociedades Bíblicas en América Latina, 1960. Renovado © Sociedades Bíblicas Unidas, 1988.

slideScriptures.text_en:
3 But he said unto them, Have ye not read what David did, when he was an hungred, and they that were with him;
4 How he entered into the house of God, and did eat the shewbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests?
slideScriptures.text_es:
3 Pero él les dijo: ¿No habéis leído lo que hizo David, cuando él y los que con él estaban tuvieron hambre;
4 cómo entró en la casa de Dios, y comió los panes de la proposición, que no les era lícito comer ni a él ni a los que con él estaban, sino solamente a los sacerdotes?
slideScriptures.copyright: Texto bíblico: Reina-Valera 1960 ® © Sociedades Bíblicas en América Latina, 1960. Renovado © Sociedades Bíblicas Unidas, 1988.

slideScriptures.text_en:
5 Or have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?
6 But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple.
slideScriptures.text_es:
5 ¿O no habéis leído en la ley, cómo en el día de reposo los sacerdotes en el templo profanan el día de reposo, y son sin culpa?
6 Pues os digo que uno mayor que el templo está aquí.
slideScriptures.copyright: Texto bíblico: Reina-Valera 1960 ® © Sociedades Bíblicas en América Latina, 1960. Renovado © Sociedades Bíblicas Unidas, 1988.

slideScriptures.text_en: For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily.
slideScriptures.text_es: Porque en él habita corporalmente toda la plenitud de la Deidad,
slideScriptures.copyright: Texto bíblico: Reina-Valera 1960 ® © Sociedades Bíblicas en América Latina, 1960. Renovado © Sociedades Bíblicas Unidas, 1988.

slideScriptures.text_en: But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.
slideScriptures.text_es: Y si supieseis qué significa: Misericordia quiero, y no sacrificio, no condenaríais a los inocentes;
slideScriptures.copyright: Texto bíblico: Reina-Valera 1960 ® © Sociedades Bíblicas en América Latina, 1960. Renovado © Sociedades Bíblicas Unidas, 1988.

slideScriptures.text_en: For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
slideScriptures.text_es: Porque misericordia quiero, y no sacrificio, y conocimiento de Dios más que holocaustos.

slideScriptures.text_en: ...Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep: for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations; that ye may know that I am the LORD that doth sanctify you.
slideScriptures.text_es: Tú hablarás a los hijos de Israel, diciendo: En verdad vosotros guardaréis mis días de reposo; porque es señal entre mí y vosotros por vuestras generaciones, para que sepáis que yo soy el Señor que os santifico.
slideScriptures.copyright: Texto bíblico: Reina-Valera 1960 ® © Sociedades Bíblicas en América Latina, 1960. Renovado © Sociedades Bíblicas Unidas, 1988.

slideScriptures.text_en:
9 And when he was departed thence, he went into their synagogue:
10 And, behold, there was a man which had his hand withered. And they asked him, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days? that they might accuse him.
slideScriptures.text_es:
9 Pasando de allí, vino a la sinagoga de ellos.
10 Y he aquí había allí uno que tenía seca una mano; y preguntaron a Jesús, para poder acusarle: ¿Es lícito sanar en el día de reposo?
slideScriptures.copyright: Texto bíblico: Reina-Valera 1960 ® © Sociedades Bíblicas en América Latina, 1960. Renovado © Sociedades Bíblicas Unidas, 1988.

slideScriptures.text_en:
11 And he said unto them, What man shall there be among you, that shall have one sheep, and if it fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out?
12 How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.
13 Then saith he to the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched it forth; and it was restored whole, like as the other.
slideScriptures.text_es:
11 El les dijo: ¿Qué hombre habrá de vosotros, que tenga una oveja, y si ésta cayere en un hoyo en día de reposo, no le eche mano, y la levante?
12 Pues ¿cuánto más vale un hombre que una oveja? Por consiguiente, es lícito hacer el bien en los días de reposo.
13 Entonces dijo a aquel hombre: Extiende tu mano. Y él la extendió, y le fue restaurada sana como la otra.

17 That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying,
18 Behold my servant, whom I have chosen; my beloved, in whom my soul is well pleased: I will put my spirit upon him, and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles.
19 He shall not strive, nor cry; neither shall any man hear his voice in the streets.
slideScriptures.text_es:
17 para que se cumpliese lo dicho por el profeta Isaías, cuando dijo:
18 He aquí mi siervo, a quien he escogido; Mi Amado, en quien se agrada mi alma; Pondré mi Espíritu sobre él, Y a los gentiles anunciará juicio.

slideScriptures.text_en:
20 A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.
21 And in his name shall the Gentiles trust.
slideScriptures.text_es:
20 La caña cascada no quebrará, Y el pábilo que humea no apagará, Hasta que saque a victoria el juicio.
21 Y en su nombre esperarán los gentiles.

manuscript.title: The Lord of the Sabbath
manuscript.html:
THE LORD OF THE SABBATH

The Lord Who Gives Rest, Has Authority, and Restores

Matthew 11:28–30 | Matthew 12:1–21 (KJV)
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The Lord Who Gives Rest
manuscript.html: INTRODUCTION: THE LORD WHO GIVES REST
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Matthew 11:28-30
manuscript.html:
Matthew 11:28–30

Matthew 11:28 (KJV) Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

Matthew 11:29 (KJV) Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.

Matthew 11:30 (KJV) For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: You can rest your body and still carry the burden.
manuscript.html:
We often associate rest with taking a break, getting away from our responsibilities, or having an opportunity to do nothing. But there is a difference between resting physically and finding rest for your soul.

You can rest your body and still have a troubled mind. You can stop working and still be carrying the same burdens.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Jesus is offering something greater than physical rest. He is offering rest for the soul.
manuscript.html:
Jesus is offering something greater than physical rest. He is offering rest for the soul.

Notice that Jesus doesn't begin by telling them to change their circumstances. He says, "Come unto me."

And then He says something interesting: Take my yoke upon you.

A yoke represents service and submission. Jesus is not offering a life without responsibility, but a life under His direction.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Rest under His direction
manuscript.html: • Rest is not always the absence of responsibility. Sometimes it is learning whose authority you are living under.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Rest under His direction
manuscript.html: • Not every burden we carry is one that God has placed upon us.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Rest under His direction
manuscript.html: • Christ invites us to exchange the weight of our own understanding for the rest that comes through learning from Him.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The Lord who gives rest is the Lord of the Sabbath.
manuscript.html:
Now, what I find interesting is that immediately after this invitation to rest, Matthew introduces Jesus as the Lord of the Sabbath.

The Sabbath was the day of rest established by God. Yet the religious leaders had developed an understanding of its restrictions that led them to condemn people who were not guilty.

And Jesus is about to show them that they have misunderstood something about the very God whose commandments they claim to defend.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The Sabbath Was Established by God
manuscript.html: 1. THE SABBATH WAS ESTABLISHED BY GOD
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Exodus 20:8
manuscript.html:
Exodus 20:8

Exodus 20:8 (KJV) Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The Sabbath was given by God, not invented by the Pharisees.
manuscript.html:
The Sabbath was not something the Pharisees invented. It was established by God, who commanded Israel to rest on the seventh day.

It was connected to creation, but it was also a reminder of their deliverance from Egypt.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Deuteronomy 5:15
manuscript.html:
Deuteronomy 5:15

Deuteronomy 5:15 (KJV) And remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt, and that the LORD thy God brought thee out thence through a mighty hand and by a stretched out arm: therefore the LORD thy God commanded thee to keep the sabbath day.

Israel had been in bondage, serving under Pharaoh. But God delivered them, and the Sabbath became a part of their covenant life with Him.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The Sabbath reminded Israel of the God who created them, delivered them, and gave them rest.
manuscript.html: The Sabbath reminded Israel of the God who created them, delivered them, and gave them rest.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: What the Sabbath revealed
manuscript.html: • The Sabbath was holy because God established it.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: What the Sabbath revealed
manuscript.html: • It was a commandment, but it also reflected God's provision for His people.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: What the Sabbath revealed
manuscript.html: • The problem in Matthew 12 was not the Sabbath itself, but the Pharisees' misunderstanding of its proper application.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: David: When Mercy Meets Human Need
manuscript.html: 2. DAVID: WHEN MERCY MEETS HUMAN NEED
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Matthew 12:1-2
manuscript.html:
Matthew 12:1–4

Matthew 12:1 (KJV) At that time Jesus went on the sabbath day through the corn; and his disciples were an hungred, and began to pluck the ears of corn and to eat.

Matthew 12:2 (KJV) But when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto him, Behold, thy disciples do that which is not lawful to do upon the sabbath day.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Matthew 12:3-4
manuscript.html:
Matthew 12:3 (KJV) But he said unto them, Have ye not read what David did, when he was an hungred, and they that were with him;

Matthew 12:4 (KJV) How he entered into the house of God, and did eat the shewbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests?
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Human need meets a narrow interpretation of the Sabbath.
manuscript.html:
The disciples were hungry, and as they walked through the field, they began gathering grain to eat.

Under Deuteronomy 23:25, gathering grain by hand was permitted. The Pharisees' objection was that they were doing it on the Sabbath.

Jesus responds by bringing them back to David.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: David, Ahimelech, and the bread reserved for the priests.
manuscript.html:
The story of David (1 Samuel 21:1–6)

David was fleeing from Saul when he came to Ahimelech the priest seeking food.

There was no ordinary bread available, only the consecrated shewbread, which according to Leviticus 24:9 was reserved for the priests.

Yet Ahimelech gave David the bread.

Jesus uses this account to challenge the Pharisees' condemnation of His hungry disciples.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Why is this significant?
manuscript.html: Why is this significant?
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Why David's story matters
manuscript.html: • David's hunger was a genuine human need.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Why David's story matters
manuscript.html: • The shewbread was holy, and Jesus acknowledges that its use was ordinarily restricted.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Why David's story matters
manuscript.html: • Yet Jesus appeals to this account to expose the failure of the Pharisees to understand mercy.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: God's holiness and His mercy are not in opposition to one another.
manuscript.html:
God's holiness and His mercy are not in opposition to one another.

This doesn't mean that human need gives us permission to disregard God's commandments. Rather, Jesus is showing that their interpretation of the Law has failed to recognize what God desires.

Application: We must be careful not to become so concerned with preserving our understanding of religious practices that we lose sight of the people God has called us to serve.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The Priests: Service and Authority
manuscript.html: 3. THE PRIESTS: SERVICE AND AUTHORITY
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Matthew 12:5-6
manuscript.html:
Matthew 12:5–6

Matthew 12:5 (KJV) Or have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?

Matthew 12:6 (KJV) But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The priests served on the Sabbath and remained blameless.
manuscript.html:
Jesus now gives another example, this time concerning the priests.

According to Numbers 28:9–10, the priests were commanded to perform additional sacrifices on the Sabbath.

While Israel rested from ordinary work, the priests continued their service in the temple.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Why does Jesus say they profane the Sabbath but remain blameless?
manuscript.html:
Why does Jesus say they profane the Sabbath but remain blameless?

Because the work they performed was commanded by God Himself.

What would ordinarily be considered work on the Sabbath was required as part of their service to God.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The priests were blameless
manuscript.html: • The priests were not disobeying God. They were fulfilling His commandments.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The priests were blameless
manuscript.html: • Their service did not make them guilty.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The priests were blameless
manuscript.html:
• Jesus demonstrates that the Pharisees' rigid understanding of Sabbath restrictions was incomplete.

But then Jesus makes an even greater declaration.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: One greater than the temple is here.
manuscript.html:
Matthew 12:6 (KJV) That in this place is one greater than the temple.

The temple was the center of Israel's worship, the place associated with God's presence among His people.

Yet Jesus declares that One greater than the temple is standing before them.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: If service to the temple was permitted on the Sabbath, how much greater is the authority of the One who is greater than the temple?
manuscript.html: If service to the temple was permitted on the Sabbath, how much greater is the authority of the One who is greater than the temple?
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Colossians 2:9
manuscript.html:
Colossians 2:9

Colossians 2:9 (KJV) For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily.

The Pharisees were defending their understanding of what belonged to God, while failing to recognize the revelation of God standing before them in Christ.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Mercy Over Sacrifice: The Heart of God
manuscript.html: 4. MERCY OVER SACRIFICE: THE HEART OF GOD
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Matthew 12:7
manuscript.html:
Matthew 12:7

Matthew 12:7 (KJV) But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.

Jesus quotes Hosea 6:6.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Hosea 6:6
manuscript.html:
Hosea 6:6

Hosea 6:6 (KJV) For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Religious practice cannot replace mercy and knowing God.
manuscript.html:
God was not rejecting the sacrificial system that He Himself established. He was confronting people whose religious practices were disconnected from genuine faithfulness to Him.

They could offer sacrifices while neglecting the mercy and knowledge of God.

And now Jesus applies this principle to the Pharisees.

He tells them that if they understood what God meant by mercy, they would not have condemned the guiltless.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Notice that Jesus doesn't say His disciples are guilty but forgiven. He declares them guiltless.
manuscript.html: Notice that Jesus doesn't say His disciples are guilty but forgiven. He declares them guiltless.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Mercy and obedience belong together
manuscript.html: • Religious observance cannot replace genuine obedience to God's will.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Mercy and obedience belong together
manuscript.html: • God's commandments should never become an excuse for neglecting mercy.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Mercy and obedience belong together
manuscript.html:
• It is possible to know the commandments of God and still misunderstand the character of the God who gave them.

Holiness matters. Obedience matters. But neither should be separated from the mercy and goodness of God.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The Lord of the Sabbath Has Authority
manuscript.html: 5. THE LORD OF THE SABBATH HAS AUTHORITY
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Matthew 12:8
manuscript.html:
Matthew 12:8

Matthew 12:8 (KJV) For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The Son of man is Lord even of the Sabbath.
manuscript.html:
Everything Jesus has said leads to this declaration.

He has referenced David, the priests, the temple, and the mercy of God.

Now He identifies His own authority.

The Sabbath was established by God. It was holy unto the Lord.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Exodus 31:13
manuscript.html:
Exodus 31:13

Exodus 31:13 (KJV) ...Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep: for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations; that ye may know that I am the LORD that doth sanctify you.

Notice that God calls them my sabbaths.

Yet Jesus declares Himself Lord even of the Sabbath.

He is not merely giving His opinion concerning the Law. He is declaring His authority over what God Himself established.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Christ has authority
manuscript.html: • Christ is greater than the temple.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Christ has authority
manuscript.html: • Christ is Lord of the Sabbath.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Christ has authority
manuscript.html:
• Christ has authority to declare what is lawful and to reveal the purpose of God's commandments.

Now connect this back to Matthew 11.

The One who says, "I will give you rest," is the very One who declares Himself Lord of the Sabbath.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The Lord of the Sabbath has authority not only to command rest, but to give rest.
manuscript.html:
The Lord of the Sabbath has authority not only to command rest, but to give rest.

And Jesus is about to demonstrate His authority through an act of restoration.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The Lord of the Sabbath Restores
manuscript.html: 6. THE LORD OF THE SABBATH RESTORES
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Matthew 12:9-10
manuscript.html:
Matthew 12:9–13

Matthew 12:9 (KJV) And when he was departed thence, he went into their synagogue:

Matthew 12:10 (KJV) And, behold, there was a man which had his hand withered. And they asked him, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days? that they might accuse him.

manuscript.title: Matthew 12:11-13
manuscript.html:
Matthew 12:11 (KJV) And he said unto them, What man shall there be among you, that shall have one sheep, and if it fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out?

Matthew 12:12 (KJV) How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.

Matthew 12:13 (KJV) Then saith he to the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched it forth; and it was restored whole, like as the other.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: Jesus demonstrates what He has just taught.
manuscript.html:
Now Jesus moves from teaching about the Sabbath to demonstrating what He has been teaching.

There is a man with a withered hand, and the Pharisees ask whether healing is lawful on the Sabbath.

But notice their intention.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: That they might accuse him.
manuscript.html:
Matthew 12:10 (KJV) That they might accuse him.

They were more interested in finding a reason to accuse Jesus than in seeing the man restored.

Jesus answers by asking whether they would rescue a sheep that had fallen into a pit on the Sabbath.

If they recognized the importance of rescuing an animal, how much more should they recognize the value of restoring a person?
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The Sabbath was never intended to make doing good unlawful.
manuscript.html: The Sabbath was never intended to make doing good unlawful.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The Lord of the Sabbath restores
manuscript.html: • The Pharisees were looking for grounds to accuse.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The Lord of the Sabbath restores
manuscript.html: • Jesus was demonstrating the mercy of God.
manuscript.notes: Full original manuscript below; advance manually.

manuscript.title: The Lord of the Sabbath restores
manuscript.html:
• The Lord of the Sabbath did not merely defend His authority. He used His authority to restore.

And notice that Jesus doesn't simply explain what is lawful.

# THE LORD OF THE SABBATH
### The Lord Who Gives Rest, Has Authority, and Restores
**Matthew 11:28–30 | Matthew 12:1–21 (KJV)**

## INTRODUCTION: THE LORD WHO GIVES REST

**Matthew 11:28–30**

***28 Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.***

***29 Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.***

***30 For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.***

We often associate rest with taking a break, getting away from our responsibilities, or having an opportunity to do nothing. But there is a difference between resting physically and finding rest for your soul.

You can rest your body and still have a troubled mind. You can stop working and still be carrying the same burdens.

**Jesus is offering something greater than physical rest. He is offering rest for the soul.**

Notice that Jesus doesn't begin by telling them to change their circumstances. He says, **"Come unto me."**

And then He says something interesting: *Take my yoke upon you.*

A yoke represents service and submission. Jesus is not offering a life without responsibility, but a life under His direction.

- **Rest is not always the absence of responsibility. Sometimes it is learning whose authority you are living under.**
- Not every burden we carry is one that God has placed upon us.
- Christ invites us to exchange the weight of our own understanding for the rest that comes through learning from Him.

Now, what I find interesting is that immediately after this invitation to rest, Matthew introduces Jesus as the **Lord of the Sabbath**.

The Sabbath was the day of rest established by God. Yet the religious leaders had developed an understanding of its restrictions that led them to condemn people who were not guilty.

And Jesus is about to show them that they have misunderstood something about the very God whose commandments they claim to defend.

## 1. THE SABBATH WAS ESTABLISHED BY GOD

**Exodus 20:8**

***Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.***

The Sabbath was not something the Pharisees invented. It was established by God, who commanded Israel to rest on the seventh day.

It was connected to creation, but it was also a reminder of their deliverance from Egypt.

**Deuteronomy 5:15**

***And remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt, and that the LORD thy God brought thee out thence through a mighty hand and by a stretched out arm: therefore the LORD thy God commanded thee to keep the sabbath day.***

Israel had been in bondage, serving under Pharaoh. But God delivered them, and the Sabbath became a part of their covenant life with Him.

**The Sabbath reminded Israel of the God who created them, delivered them, and gave them rest.**

- The Sabbath was holy because God established it.
- It was a commandment, but it also reflected God's provision for His people.
- **The problem in Matthew 12 was not the Sabbath itself, but the Pharisees' misunderstanding of its proper application.**

## 2. DAVID: WHEN MERCY MEETS HUMAN NEED

**Matthew 12:1–4**

***1 At that time Jesus went on the sabbath day through the corn; and his disciples were an hungred, and began to pluck the ears of corn and to eat.***

***2 But when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto him, Behold, thy disciples do that which is not lawful to do upon the sabbath day.***

***3 But he said unto them, Have ye not read what David did, when he was an hungred, and they that were with him;***

***4 How he entered into the house of God, and did eat the shewbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests?***

The disciples were hungry, and as they walked through the field, they began gathering grain to eat.

Under Deuteronomy 23:25, gathering grain by hand was permitted. The Pharisees' objection was that they were doing it on the Sabbath.

Jesus responds by bringing them back to David.

### The story of David (1 Samuel 21:1–6)

David was fleeing from Saul when he came to Ahimelech the priest seeking food.

There was no ordinary bread available, only the consecrated shewbread, which according to Leviticus 24:9 was reserved for the priests.

Yet Ahimelech gave David the bread.

Jesus uses this account to challenge the Pharisees' condemnation of His hungry disciples.

**Why is this significant?**

- David's hunger was a genuine human need.
- The shewbread was holy, and Jesus acknowledges that its use was ordinarily restricted.
- Yet Jesus appeals to this account to expose the failure of the Pharisees to understand mercy.

**God's holiness and His mercy are not in opposition to one another.**

This doesn't mean that human need gives us permission to disregard God's commandments. Rather, Jesus is showing that their interpretation of the Law has failed to recognize what God desires.

**Application:** We must be careful not to become so concerned with preserving our understanding of religious practices that we lose sight of the people God has called us to serve.

## 3. THE PRIESTS: SERVICE AND AUTHORITY

**Matthew 12:5–6**

***5 Or have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?***

***6 But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple.***

Jesus now gives another example, this time concerning the priests.

According to Numbers 28:9–10, the priests were commanded to perform additional sacrifices on the Sabbath.

While Israel rested from ordinary work, the priests continued their service in the temple.

**Why does Jesus say they profane the Sabbath but remain blameless?**

Because the work they performed was commanded by God Himself.

What would ordinarily be considered work on the Sabbath was required as part of their service to God.

- The priests were not disobeying God. They were fulfilling His commandments.
- Their service did not make them guilty.
- **Jesus demonstrates that the Pharisees' rigid understanding of Sabbath restrictions was incomplete.**

But then Jesus makes an even greater declaration.

***That in this place is one greater than the temple.***

The temple was the center of Israel's worship, the place associated with God's presence among His people.

Yet Jesus declares that One greater than the temple is standing before them.

**If service to the temple was permitted on the Sabbath, how much greater is the authority of the One who is greater than the temple?**

**Colossians 2:9**

***For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily.***

The Pharisees were defending their understanding of what belonged to God, while failing to recognize the revelation of God standing before them in Christ.

## 4. MERCY OVER SACRIFICE: THE HEART OF GOD

**Matthew 12:7**

***But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.***

Jesus quotes Hosea 6:6.

**Hosea 6:6**

***For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.***

God was not rejecting the sacrificial system that He Himself established. He was confronting people whose religious practices were disconnected from genuine faithfulness to Him.

They could offer sacrifices while neglecting the mercy and knowledge of God.

And now Jesus applies this principle to the Pharisees.

He tells them that if they understood what God meant by mercy, they would not have condemned the guiltless.

**Notice that Jesus doesn't say His disciples are guilty but forgiven. He declares them guiltless.**

- Religious observance cannot replace genuine obedience to God's will.
- God's commandments should never become an excuse for neglecting mercy.
- **It is possible to know the commandments of God and still misunderstand the character of the God who gave them.**

Holiness matters. Obedience matters. But neither should be separated from the mercy and goodness of God.

## 5. THE LORD OF THE SABBATH HAS AUTHORITY

**Matthew 12:8**

***For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.***

Everything Jesus has said leads to this declaration.

He has referenced David, the priests, the temple, and the mercy of God.

Now He identifies His own authority.

The Sabbath was established by God. It was holy unto the Lord.

**Exodus 31:13**

***...Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep: for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations; that ye may know that I am the LORD that doth sanctify you.***

Notice that God calls them *my sabbaths*.

Yet Jesus declares Himself **Lord even of the Sabbath**.

He is not merely giving His opinion concerning the Law. He is declaring His authority over what God Himself established.

- **Christ is greater than the temple.**
- **Christ is Lord of the Sabbath.**
- **Christ has authority to declare what is lawful and to reveal the purpose of God's commandments.**

Now connect this back to Matthew 11.

The One who says, *"I will give you rest,"* is the very One who declares Himself Lord of the Sabbath.

**The Lord of the Sabbath has authority not only to command rest, but to give rest.**

And Jesus is about to demonstrate His authority through an act of restoration.

## 6. THE LORD OF THE SABBATH RESTORES

**Matthew 12:9–13**

***9 And when he was departed thence, he went into their synagogue:***

***10 And, behold, there was a man which had his hand withered. And they asked him, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days? that they might accuse him.***

***11 And he said unto them, What man shall there be among you, that shall have one sheep, and if it fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out?***

***12 How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.***

***13 Then saith he to the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched it forth; and it was restored whole, like as the other.***

Now Jesus moves from teaching about the Sabbath to demonstrating what He has been teaching.

There is a man with a withered hand, and the Pharisees ask whether healing is lawful on the Sabbath.

But notice their intention.

***That they might accuse him.***

They were more interested in finding a reason to accuse Jesus than in seeing the man restored.

Jesus answers by asking whether they would rescue a sheep that had fallen into a pit on the Sabbath.

If they recognized the importance of rescuing an animal, how much more should they recognize the value of restoring a person?

**The Sabbath was never intended to make doing good unlawful.**

- The Pharisees were looking for grounds to accuse.
- Jesus was demonstrating the mercy of God.
- **The Lord of the Sabbath did not merely defend His authority. He used His authority to restore.**

And notice that Jesus doesn't simply explain what is lawful.

He heals the man.

The very thing they were questioning becomes the demonstration of His teaching.

## 7. THE LORD OF THE SABBATH IS REJECTED

**Matthew 12:14–16**

***14 Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.***

***15 But when Jesus knew it, he withdrew himself from thence: and great multitudes followed him, and he healed them all;***

***16 And charged them that they should not make him known:***

There is an incredible contradiction here.

Jesus has just restored a man's hand.

Yet the religious leaders respond by planning how to destroy Him.

**They condemned an act of restoration while plotting the destruction of the One who performed it.**

And even with this opposition, Jesus continues to heal those who come to Him.

His authority was never separated from His mercy.

## 8. THE LORD OF THE SABBATH IS MEEK AND LOWLY

**Matthew 12:17–21**

***17 That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying,***

***18 Behold my servant, whom I have chosen; my beloved, in whom my soul is well pleased: I will put my spirit upon him, and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles.***

***19 He shall not strive, nor cry; neither shall any man hear his voice in the streets.***

***20 A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.***

***21 And in his name shall the Gentiles trust.***

Matthew connects the actions of Jesus to Isaiah 42:1–4.

This prophecy describes the character of God's chosen Servant.

Although He has authority, He does not pursue His mission through self-promotion or unnecessary conflict.

***A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench...***

A bruised reed is already weakened. Smoking flax describes a wick whose flame is barely burning.

Yet Christ is described as One who does not crush the weak or extinguish what is barely burning.

Think about what we have seen throughout the chapter.

- The disciples were hungry. **Jesus defended them.**
- The man had a withered hand. **Jesus restored him.**
- The Pharisees sought to destroy Him. **Jesus continued healing.**

And this brings us right back to Matthew 11:29.

***...for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.***

**The One who has authority over the Sabbath is also the One who is meek and lowly in heart.**

His authority is not contrary to His mercy.

And His gentleness does not diminish His power.

---

## CONCLUSION: THE LORD WHO GIVES REST

We began with the invitation of Jesus in Matthew 11.

***Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.***

And throughout Matthew 12, we have seen the authority and character of the One making that invitation.

He is greater than the temple.

He is Lord of the Sabbath.

He has the authority to defend the guiltless, to declare what is lawful, and to restore those in need.

Yet the same Lord who possesses this authority describes Himself as meek and lowly in heart.

**The Lord of the Sabbath does not simply have authority over a day of rest. He has authority to give rest to the soul.**

And I think that teaches us something important about our relationship with God.

Our rest is not found in the absence of His authority, but in learning to live under it.

Because when we understand who He is, we discover that His commandments are not disconnected from His goodness, His holiness is not disconnected from His mercy, and His authority is not disconnected from His love.

**The One who calls us to obedience is the same One who invites us to find rest in Him.**

And if we claim to follow Him, then our lives should reflect not only His commandments, but also His character.

**Because we cannot claim to know the Lord of the Sabbath while refusing to learn from the mercy of the Lord who gives rest.**
